title: Adaptive Throughput Manager: Multi-metric Autoscaling with Safety Windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement an autoscaling policy engine for Dedicated fleets that balances throughput guarantees and unit cost by combining multiple target signals, bounded scaling actions, and explicit safety windows. This ticket defines the algorithm, config surface, safety limits, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the first implementation.
design_notes:
Target metrics: (1) tokens_per_second_per_gpu (primary throughput), normalized per model class; (2) request_queue_length (short-term backlog); (3) p95_generation_latency (service-level safety); (4) gpu_utilization (hardware signal); (5) cost_rate (tokens-per-dollar estimated). The engine will compute a composite scaling score using weighted normalized metrics. Scaling algorithm: layered approach -

- Short-term reactive layer: damped proportional-integral controller (PI) with exponential decay on the integral term to avoid windup. Integral age parameter configurable per fleet. Proportional term primarily driven by tokens_per_second_per_gpu vs target.
- Momentum limiter: per-minute gradient cap that bounds the percent change in replica count (configurable default +25%/-15% per minute) to avoid oscillations.
- Predictive smoothing: optional lightweight AR(1) predictor on queue_length to pre-warm capacity for sudden bursts (toggle per project).
- Cost-aware throttling: when cost_rate exceeds configured budget threshold, scale decisions down-prioritize non-critical tenants or shift low-priority workloads to fractional models/quantized variants (via policy tags).

Safety limits and rules:
- Hard min_replicas and max_replicas per fleet; default min=2, max derived from committed capacity.
- Scale-down cooldown = 300s by default; scale-up cooldown = 30s default. These are overridable per-customer policy.
- Emergency brake: if p99_latency > emergency_threshold or error_rate spikes 5x baseline, auto-disable scaling-to-zero and trigger rollback to last-known-good replica set.
- Conservative backoff on oscillation detection: if the algorithm reverses direction twice within a configured window, enter a 'stabilize' mode for 10 minutes where only minimal safe rescales allowed.

Config surface/API:
- AutoscalePolicy {target_tokens_per_gpu, target_p95_latency, weights:{throughput,latency,utilization,cost}, min_replicas, max_replicas, scale_up_cooldown_s, scale_down_cooldown_s, gradient_cap_pct_per_min, predictive_enabled, emergency_thresholds, priority_tiers}
- Admin UI: slider presets (Aggressive / Balanced / Conservative) and a sandbox simulator to replay historical traffic.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Autoscaler computes a stable replica count for synthetic traces covering ramp(0->100%) in 10min, spike(5x for 30s), and step-down. Replica oscillation must be <2 reversals over 20 minutes in balanced preset.
2) When cost_rate toggled to budget-exceeded, autoscaler must prefer scale-down of low-priority pools and maintain SLOs for high-priority pools.
3) Emergency brake triggers and a rollback triggerable via API and console when p99_latency breaches threshold.
4) Expose metrics: desired_replicas, current_replicas, composite_scale_score, individual_signal_contributions, last_scale_time, oscillation_count.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for PI controller, gradient cap, predictive smoothing.
- Integration harness: run against recorded production traces in sandbox cluster with adjustable commit size.
- Canary rollout: enable on 2 non-critical fleets (internal dev + staging customer) for 2 weeks, monitor stability metrics and runbook alerts.

Observability and runbook:
- Dashboards: per-fleet autoscale panel, signal contribution heatmap, cost vs throughput chart.
- Alerts: scale_event_rate_anomaly, oscillation_detected, emergency_brake_engaged.
- Runbook steps for emergency_brake: A) pin desired_replicas, B) notify on-call, C) roll back runtime config.
tasks: Define autoscalePolicy API proto and console UI knobs
Implement composite signal collector and normalizer
Implement PI controller with integral decay and gradient cap
Add emergency brake and rollback hooks
Create sandbox simulation harness and run tests
acceptance_criteria: Stable behavior for synthetic ramp/spike/step tests
Cost-aware decisions degrade lower-priority pools first
Emergency brake triggers and rollback works via API and Console
implementation_notes: Start by shipping the composite signal normalizer (no-op default weights) so teams can experiment with weights without affecting live decisions. Keep policy evaluation idempotent and side-effect free: compute desired_replicas in-memory, then execute a single compare-and-set to the fleet controller. Persist policy versions for auditing. Provide a simulation end-to-end that can be run in CI against sample traces.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: oscillation on mixed tenant workloads -> Mitigation: gradient cap + stabilize mode
Risk: noisy GPU utilization signal -> Mitigation: use median-smoothed window and prefer tokens_per_second for primary decision
Risk: cost budget misconfigurations -> Mitigation: conservative defaults and warn on aggressive presets
